## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f4fc5ea9ef745844ea53e28ac399fa53f8f62f17`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-platform/references/bootstrap.md, skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md + none

Read on `origin/main` (the PR's base `34c05229`; main has since moved to `b5f2f516`, which touches none of these files and not `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`): `composeStacks`, `composeBuiltStacks`, `ComposeStacksOptionsSchema.manifest`, `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES`, `SINGLE_APP_COMPOSE_REMEDY`, `singleAppFinding`, `validateSingleApp`, `collectComposedSingleAppErrors`, `flatSingleAppFinding`, `residualSingleAppFinding`, `StackRefusalError`, `StackSingleAppViolationError`; `examples/app-multi-package/objectstack.config.ts` and its two packages; `docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`; card #32977 with every comment (fold 6846119916, dev report 6884932864); card #33135 with its comment.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: none moves. The diff is skill prose and a changeset; no schema, no runtime, no gate script. What the prose teaches is checked against the accept set that is already on main (④).
- Public surface: the `@objectstack/skills` published text only (two files). Right.
- Gates: the head's check-runs are the verdicts. At review 18 completed success, 18 skipped, none failed, and 9 still in progress (`Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`). The token and line ratchets and the skill-doc checks ride the lint lanes still running; the merge waits on them green. This record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32977-skills-suite-composes-under-preserve.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. Matches the repo's convention for skill-text corrections (the last five `docs(skills)` merges on main carry the same line). Right.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset: no published key is added, removed or narrowed. Right. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation, ADR-0019 left to #33135: right. Fold 6846119916 row 2 and #33135 name one sentence of ADR-0019's "Enforced for modules" note ("Two shapes are not judged ... a flat `composeStacks` ... and a hand-built `packages[]` body"), a governed ADR surface, and one sentence wants one owner. Escalated, not a finding on this diff: #33135's Expected names only the hand-built body half, and this PR carries `Fixes #32977`, so the merge closes the card that holds row 2. The seat writes onto #33135, before or at this merge, that the flat-composition half of the sentence is false too since PR #32898 and the PR for #33135 rewrites the whole sentence; otherwise row 2 is lost.
- Deviation, `resolveArtifactCollections` not taught: right. 6846119916 says the remedy "can" name it; the card's Work asks for the `preserve` remedy, and an author composes with `composeStacks`, not with the runtime reader.
- Deviation, no HTML-comment trailer, model-free commit trailer, no merge of the moved main: process lines for the seat; none bears on the contract.
- Deviation, the in-file cuts: judged in ④.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-platform/references/bootstrap.md`, § Multi-App Composition, against the card's Work items 1 and 2 and `stack.zod.ts` on main:

- "A suite (an app package plus module packages, one app each) composes with `composeStacks(stacks, { manifest: 'preserve' })`, which keeps each package's own id": holds. `SINGLE_APP_COMPOSE_REMEDY` says the same words; under `'preserve'` each input with a manifest is assembled into a body of its own and registered under its own id, so a one-app-per-package suite leaves no residual app (`collectComposedSingleAppErrors` doc). The qualifier "one app each" with each being a package is what keeps the residual rule from biting, so the sentence does not over-promise.
- "(`examples/app-multi-package`)": holds. Line 68 of the config is `composeStacks([ordersStack, coreStack], { manifest: 'preserve' })`, and the two inputs are a `type: 'app'` package (`com.example.multi.core`) and a `type: 'module'` package (`com.example.multi.orders`). The old "No app in this repo uses it" is gone. Work item 2 done.
- "A flat `manifest` (`'last'`, the default, `'first'` or an index) keeps one": holds. The schema is `z.union([z.enum(['first', 'last', 'preserve']), z.number().int().min(0)]).default('last')`; the three non-preserve values are the pick-one set the option doc names.
- "so two or more apps under one `app` or `module` package id are refused": holds on the exact condition. `flatSingleAppFinding` refuses when the composed manifest's `type` is in `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES` (`app`, `module`) and the composed `apps` holds more than one entry; a kept manifest of any other type, or one app in all, passes. The sentence names both the package-type gate and the count.
- "(`STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`, 422)": holds. `StackSingleAppViolationError.code = 'STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION'`, `status = 422` from `StackRefusalError`, thrown by `composeBuiltStacks` on the `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` result. Work item 1 done.
- Tried to break it: a single input (`stacks.length === 1` returns it untouched) is not a composition and not a suite; a flat composition whose input carries `packages[]` is judged by the residual rule instead, and is still refused in the case the sentence describes; under `'preserve'` an input with no manifest can still be refused (residual app). None of these makes a taught sentence false: the text claims nothing about them.
- The first paragraph's cuts ("this is how real multi-app composition happens", "equal the physical table name") lose no rule: the table-name rule stands in `objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` § Object naming ("equals the physical table name"), and "globally unique `name`" plus "use it directly" keep the instruction.
- Other cuts ("(moved verbatim from SKILL.md)", "(traditional)", "(key becomes name) ... for readability", "Use barrel exports to keep config clean:", "A minimal but complete project from scratch:", the `stack.zod.ts` pointer): each restates its heading, the sentence above the block, or `references/_index.md` (which lists `stack.zod.ts`). "read the schema before reaching for it" went with the false claim it hedged. No other file in the tree quotes the removed title or sentence. No rule lost.

`skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`, § App Navigation, against fold 6846119916 row 1:

- "the suite composes with `composeStacks(stacks, { manifest: 'preserve' })`, which serves each app under its own package id; a flat composition puts them under one and is refused": holds. It is `SINGLE_APP_COMPOSE_REMEDY` ("a flat composition puts every app back under one") in the section's words; in a suite the kept manifest is an `app` or `module` package, so the unqualified "is refused" is true for the case the paragraph is about. "served under that module's package id" folded into "serves each app under its own package id", and "gone when it is disabled" is kept. Row 1 done.
- `requiresObject` / `requiresService` note shortened: the behaviour (an item hides when the optional object or service is missing) and the prohibition ("never hard-code conditional UI") both stay. No rule lost.
- Finding 1, nit: the `subforms` example's comment cut removes this file's only mention of the `relationshipField` key. The behaviour stays taught (the paragraph under the list: "The relationship FK and grid columns are derived from the child object's metadata in every case"), the old comment taught no FK override either, and the key is taught in `objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` and `objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md`. No effect on correctness; accepted as a deviation.

No must-fix, no should-fix. One nit, accepted. The ADR-0019 relay onto #33135 is the seat's (③), not this diff's.

## Correction: contract-review tier

The contract-review record(s) 6885186638 on this PR say `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the seat adopted them as "isolated sub-agent at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER". **That is wrong.** The seat launched the reviewing sub-agent without the tier, so it ran at the seat's own default tier, not at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat found this on its own audit. The review was still isolated and adversarial, and its findings stand as an off-tier review. They are not the at-tier record AGENTS.md and the in-seat review ruling require.

The seat re-runs the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this PR's head and posts that record here. Until it does, this PR has no at-tier record.
